confirmed_failure.main_process_impact: byte-identical Git trees could require repository-wide index regeneration after checkout, worktree creation, or fast-forward

root_cause.filesystem_observation: nested file last_updated fields are derived from stat().st_mtime
root_cause.defect: the folder content_hash excluded only top-level last_updated and therefore hashed nested filesystem timestamps
root_cause.workflow_amplifier: stale-result and agent guidance prescribed all-folder regeneration, while the closeout workflow did not make the final repository mutation cutoff explicit

implemented_resolution.hash_contract: recursively exclude every last_updated field while retaining per-file content_hash values and deterministic structural projections
implemented_resolution.scheduled_contract: run all-folder freshness as a read-only Monday audit; never schedule index writes or commits
closeout_contract: freeze owned logs, task and handoff state, local evidence, and the pre-commit receipt
refresh affected indexes once as the final repository write
commit and audit an immutable candidate
keep PR, hosted-check, and merge facts in GitHub and the external handoff
create an explicit repair candidate only for a material post-push defect
implemented_resolution.reason_structural_guards_retained: they validate registry membership and link structure, not the 32-folder freshness watermark

regression.observation: moving one unchanged Python file mtime from 2020 to 2021 changes its display date but not the folder content_hash

immutable_closeout.final_repository_write: one-time regeneration of the 32 maintained indexes after this evidence and the handoff receipt are frozen
post_commit_acceptance: 32/32 indexes current in the candidate worktree
32/32 indexes current in a fresh detached worktree at the exact candidate commit
required hosted checks pass on the unchanged head
squash merge tree equals the reviewed candidate tree
primary main reports 32/32 indexes current after fast-forward
immutable_closeout.post_commit_results_location: GitHub checks, merge metadata, and the external final handoff; no same-candidate backwrite
